audit_status.source_base: Greek Romans text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Abraham, counted righteousness/justice, David, circumcision sign, promise, trust apart from Law, life from dead.

verses.restored: What then shall we say Abraham, our forefather according to flesh, has found?

familiar.text: What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found?

modern.text: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather, has discovered?

original.text: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν ⸀εὑρηκέναι Ἀβραὰμ τὸν ⸀προπάτορα ⸀ἡμῶν κατὰ σάρκα;

verses.restored: For if Abraham was made righteous/just from works, he has boast—but not toward the Divine.

familiar.text: For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God.

modern.text: If Abraham was indeed justified by works, he had something to boast about, but not before God.

original.text: εἰ γὰρ Ἀβραὰμ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη, ἔχει καύχημα· ἀλλʼ οὐ ⸀πρὸς θεόν,

verses.restored: For what does the Scripture say? Abraham trusted the Divine, and it was counted to him as righteousness/justice.

familiar.text: For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness.

modern.text: For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”

original.text: τί γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ λέγει; Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.

verses.restored: Now to the one working, the wage is not counted according to grace but according to debt.

familiar.text: Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.

modern.text: Now the wages of the worker are not credited as a gift, but as an obligation.

original.text: τῷ δὲ ἐργαζομένῳ ὁ μισθὸς οὐ λογίζεται κατὰ χάριν ἀλλὰ κατὰ ὀφείλημα·

verses.restored: But to the one not working yet trusting upon the One making righteous/just the ungodly, that one's trust is counted as righteousness/justice.

familiar.text: But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.

modern.text: However, to the one who does not work, but believes in Him who justifies the wicked, his faith is credited as righteousness.

original.text: τῷ δὲ μὴ ἐργαζομένῳ, πιστεύοντι δὲ ἐπὶ τὸν δικαιοῦντα τὸν ἀσεβῆ, λογίζεται ἡ πίστις αὐτοῦ εἰς δικαιοσύνην,

verses.restored: Just as David also speaks of the blessedness of the human to whom the Divine counts righteousness/justice apart from works:

familiar.text: Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works,

modern.text: And David speaks likewise of the blessedness of the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:

original.text: καθάπερ καὶ Δαυὶδ λέγει τὸν μακαρισμὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ᾧ ὁ θεὸς λογίζεται δικαιοσύνην χωρὶς ἔργων·

verses.restored: Blessed/flourishing are those whose lawless deeds were released and whose sins/misalignments were covered;

familiar.text: Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered.

modern.text: “Blessed are they whose lawless acts are forgiven, whose sins are covered.

original.text: Μακάριοι ὧν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἀνομίαι καὶ ὧν ἐπεκαλύφθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι,

verses.restored: blessed/flourishing is the man to whom the Lord will certainly not count sin/misalignment.

familiar.text: Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin.

modern.text: Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never count against him.”

original.text: μακάριος ἀνὴρ ⸀οὗ οὐ μὴ λογίσηται κύριος ἁμαρτίαν.

verses.restored: Is this blessedness then upon the circumcision, or also upon the uncircumcision? For we say trust was counted to Abraham as righteousness/justice.

familiar.text: Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness.

modern.text: Is this blessing only on the circumcised, or also on the uncircumcised? We have been saying that Abraham’s faith was credited to him as righteousness.

original.text: Ὁ μακαρισμὸς οὖν οὗτος ἐπὶ τὴν περιτομὴν ἢ καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν ἀκροβυστίαν; λέγομεν ⸀γάρ· Ἐλογίσθη τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ἡ πίστις εἰς δικαιοσύνην.

verses.restored: How then was it counted? While he was in circumcision or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

familiar.text: How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

modern.text: In what context was it credited? Was it after his circumcision, or before? It was not after, but before.

original.text: πῶς οὖν ἐλογίσθη; ἐν περιτομῇ ὄντι ἢ ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ; οὐκ ἐν περιτομῇ ἀλλʼ ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ·

verses.restored: And he received a sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness/justice of the trust he had while uncircumcised, so that he might be father of all those trusting through uncircumcision, so that righteousness/justice might be counted to them,

familiar.text: And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also:

modern.text: And he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised. So then, he is the father of all who believe but are not circumcised, in order that righteousness might be credited to them.

original.text: καὶ σημεῖον ἔλαβεν περιτομῆς, σφραγῖδα τῆς δικαιοσύνης τῆς πίστεως τῆς ἐν τῇ ἀκροβυστίᾳ, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν πατέρα πάντων τῶν πιστευόντων διʼ ἀκροβυστίας, εἰς τὸ ⸀λογισθῆναι αὐτοῖς τὴν δικαιοσύνην,

verses.restored: and father of circumcision to those not only from circumcision but also walking in the footsteps of the trust of our father Abraham while uncircumcised.

familiar.text: And the father of circumcision to them who are not of the circumcision only, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had being yet uncircumcised.

modern.text: And he is also the father of the circumcised who not only are circumcised, but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised. Abraham Receives the Promise (Genesis 15:8–21)

original.text: καὶ πατέρα περιτομῆς τοῖς οὐκ ἐκ περιτομῆς μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς στοιχοῦσιν τοῖς ἴχνεσιν τῆς ⸂ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ πίστεως⸃ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἀβραάμ.

verses.restored: For the promise to Abraham or to his seed that he would be heir of the world was not through Law, but through righteousness/justice of trust.

familiar.text: For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith.

modern.text: For the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world was not given through the law, but through the righteousness that comes by faith.

original.text: Οὐ γὰρ διὰ νόμου ἡ ἐπαγγελία τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ἢ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ, τὸ κληρονόμον αὐτὸν ⸀εἶναι κόσμου, ἀλλὰ διὰ δικαιοσύνης πίστεως·

verses.restored: For if those from Law are heirs, trust has been emptied and the promise made inactive.

familiar.text: For if they which are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of none effect:

modern.text: For if those who live by the law are heirs, faith is useless and the promise is worthless,

original.text: εἰ γὰρ οἱ ἐκ νόμου κληρονόμοι, κεκένωται ἡ πίστις καὶ κατήργηται ἡ ἐπαγγελία·

verses.restored: For Law works wrath; but where there is no Law, neither is there transgression.

familiar.text: Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression.

modern.text: because the law brings wrath. And where there is no law, there is no transgression.

original.text: ὁ γὰρ νόμος ὀργὴν κατεργάζεται, οὗ ⸀δὲ οὐκ ἔστιν νόμος, οὐδὲ παράβασις.

verses.restored: Because of this it is from trust, so that it may be according to grace, so that the promise may be firm to all the seed, not only to the one from Law but also to the one from Abraham's trust, who is father of us all,

familiar.text: Therefore it is of faith, that it might be by grace; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham; who is the father of us all,

modern.text: Therefore, the promise comes by faith, so that it may rest on grace and may be guaranteed to all Abraham’s offspring—not only to those who are of the law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham. He is the father of us all.

original.text: Διὰ τοῦτο ἐκ πίστεως, ἵνα κατὰ χάριν, εἰς τὸ εἶναι βεβαίαν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν παντὶ τῷ σπέρματι, οὐ τῷ ἐκ τοῦ νόμου μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ τῷ ἐκ πίστεως Ἀβραάμ (ὅς ἐστιν πατὴρ πάντων ἡμῶν,

verses.restored: just as it is written: I have made you father of many nations—before the Divine whom he trusted, the One making the dead alive and calling the things not being as being.

familiar.text: (As it is written, I have made thee a father of many nations,) before him whom he believed, even God, who quickeneth the dead, and calleth those things which be not as though they were.

modern.text: As it is written: “I have made you a father of many nations.” He is our father in the presence of God, in whom he believed, the God who gives life to the dead and calls into being what does not yet exist.

original.text: καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν τέθεικά σε), κατέναντι οὗ ἐπίστευσεν θεοῦ τοῦ ζῳοποιοῦντος τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ καλοῦντος τὰ μὴ ὄντα ὡς ὄντα·

verses.restored: Against hope, upon hope he trusted, so that he might become father of many nations, according to what had been spoken: So shall your seed be.

familiar.text: Who against hope believed in hope, that he might become the father of many nations, according to that which was spoken, So shall thy seed be.

modern.text: Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed and so became the father of many nations, just as he had been told, “So shall your offspring be.”

original.text: ὃς παρʼ ἐλπίδα ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι ἐπίστευσεν εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι αὐτὸν πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον· Οὕτως ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου·

verses.restored: Not weakening in trust, he considered his own body already deadened, being about a hundred years old, and the deadening of Sarah's womb.

familiar.text: And being not weak in faith, he considered not his own body now dead, when he was about an hundred years old, neither yet the deadness of Sarah’s womb:

modern.text: Without weakening in his faith, he acknowledged the decrepitness of his body (since he was about a hundred years old) and the lifelessness of Sarah’s womb.

original.text: καὶ μὴ ἀσθενήσας τῇ ⸀πίστει κατενόησεν τὸ ἑαυτοῦ ⸀σῶμα νενεκρωμένον, ἑκατονταετής που ὑπάρχων, καὶ τὴν νέκρωσιν τῆς μήτρας Σάρρας,

verses.restored: He did not waver in distrust toward the promise of the Divine, but was empowered in trust, giving glory to the Divine,

familiar.text: He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God;

modern.text: Yet he did not waver through disbelief in the promise of God, but was strengthened in his faith and gave glory to God,

original.text: εἰς δὲ τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ θεοῦ οὐ διεκρίθη τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἀλλὰ ἐνεδυναμώθη τῇ πίστει, δοὺς δόξαν τῷ θεῷ

verses.restored: being fully assured that what he had promised, he was also powerful to do.

familiar.text: And being fully persuaded that, what he had promised, he was able also to perform.

modern.text: being fully persuaded that God was able to do what He had promised.

original.text: καὶ πληροφορηθεὶς ὅτι ὃ ἐπήγγελται δυνατός ἐστιν καὶ ποιῆσαι.

verses.restored: Therefore it was also counted to him as righteousness/justice.

familiar.text: And therefore it was imputed to him for righteousness.

modern.text: This is why “it was credited to him as righteousness.”

original.text: ⸀διὸ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.

verses.restored: But it was not written because of him alone that it was counted to him,

familiar.text: Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed to him;

modern.text: Now the words “it was credited to him” were written not only for Abraham,

original.text: Οὐκ ἐγράφη δὲ διʼ αὐτὸν μόνον ὅτι ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ,

verses.restored: but also because of us, to whom it is about to be counted: to those trusting upon the One who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,

familiar.text: But for us also, to whom it shall be imputed, if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead;

modern.text: but also for us, to whom righteousness will be credited—for us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.

original.text: ἀλλὰ καὶ διʼ ἡμᾶς οἷς μέλλει λογίζεσθαι, τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἐπὶ τὸν ἐγείραντα Ἰησοῦν τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν ἐκ νεκρῶν,

verses.restored: who was handed over because of our trespasses and raised because of our being made righteous/just.

familiar.text: Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification.

modern.text: He was delivered over to death for our trespasses and was raised to life for our justification.

original.text: ὃς παρεδόθη διὰ τὰ παραπτώματα ἡμῶν καὶ ἠγέρθη διὰ τὴν δικαίωσιν ἡμῶν.

translation_notes: Romans 4 is structured around Genesis 15 and Psalm 32. Abraham is made the ancestor of both circumcised and uncircumcised trust, preserving Paul's nations argument without erasing Israel's covenant story.
